question.text: Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>f</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mi>n</mi></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfenced><mo>×</mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfenced><mo>×</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mi>n</mi></mfenced><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mo>∀</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>N</mi></math>, then the number of elements in the set <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mfenced close="}" open="{" separators="|"><mrow><mi>f</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mn>1</mn></mfenced><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>f</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mn>2</mn></mfenced><mo>,</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>.</mo><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>f</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mn>6</mn></mfenced></mrow></mfenced></math> that are positive are

solution.text:
sin⁡1, sin⁡2, sin⁡3 are positive and sin⁡4, sin⁡5, sin⁡6 are negative
Hence f1, f2, f3, f5 are positive while in f4 there are exactly one negative and three positive terms. Similarly, f(6) is negative
